meta.title: Leki Bhai Ki Website
meta.tagline: A PYQ revision checklist — what the papers actually keep asking.
meta.source: Topic-frequency analysis of past BDS papers (ROS study material).
meta.tierRule: HIGH = asked 7+ times · MEDIUM = 4-6 · LOW = 3 or fewer.
dataNotes: timesAsked is the frequency the source analysis states. For a handful of topics it differs by one from the number of sittings listed beside it; both are kept exactly as written rather than silently corrected.
The source records no mark weightings, so totalMarks is 0 and each angle's marks is null until someone fills them in from the papers.
A few entries are labelled with a paper code rather than a sitting year (e.g. 2027 Code 6343) — kept verbatim.

subjects.name: Pathology
mustRead: General Path: Necrosis (esp. coagulative/caseous), acute inflammation events, wound healing, benign vs malignant, metastasis.
Hematology: Iron deficiency anaemia (lab dx), megaloblastic anaemia (lab dx), AML (FAB), CML.
Bone/Tumours: Osteosarcoma, ameloblastoma.
Clinical: Thrombosis, shock, fracture healing.

chapters.name: Cell Injury, Cell Death & Adaptation
chapters.blurb: High-yield. Necrosis and calcification are the most frequent asks.

chapters.name: Inflammation & Healing
chapters.blurb: Acute inflammation events and wound healing are almost guaranteed to appear.

chapters.name: Hemodynamics (Circulatory Disturbances)
chapters.blurb: Shock and thrombosis are the key players here.

chapters.name: Neoplasia (Tumours)
chapters.blurb: Benign vs malignant is the single most repeated question in the whole file.

chapters.name: Immunity & Genetics
chapters.blurb: Hypersensitivity carries this chapter.

chapters.name: Hematology
chapters.blurb: A major section — anaemias and leukaemias turn up in almost every paper.

chapters.name: Systemic Pathology
chapters.blurb: Specific organ diseases. Bone tumours are the most common here.

topics.name: Vitamin Deficiencies (Vit D, Vit A, Scurvy)

chapters.name: Microbiology inside the Pathology papers
chapters.blurb: The analysis flags these because they show up in the Pathology sittings too.

subjects.name: Microbiology
mustRead: General: Sterilization (autoclave).
Immunology: Hypersensitivity (Type I & IV), antigen-antibody reactions (ELISA).
Systemic Bacteriology: Pulmonary TB (lab dx), normal oral flora & dental caries.
Virology: HIV (lab dx), Hepatitis B (vaccine/dx).
Mycology: Candidiasis (oral thrush).
Parasitology: Malaria (lab dx), Entamoeba histolytica.

chapters.name: General Microbiology: Sterilization & Disinfection
chapters.blurb: The most frequently asked area here. Moist heat (autoclave) is the favourite.

chapters.name: Immunology
chapters.blurb: Hypersensitivity reactions are a must-read.

chapters.name: Systemic Bacteriology
chapters.blurb: Weighted towards dentistry — oral flora, sore throat — plus TB.

chapters.name: Virology
chapters.blurb: HIV and Hepatitis B dominate.

chapters.name: Mycology
chapters.blurb: Candidiasis is the single most important fungal topic for dental students.

chapters.name: Parasitology
chapters.blurb: Malaria and amoebiasis are the repeat offenders.

subjects.name: Pharmacology
mustRead: General: Pharmacokinetics (bioavailability), pharmacodynamics (antagonism).
CNS: Local anaesthetics (lignocaine) — most important, NSAIDs (aspirin), antiepileptics (phenytoin).
Chemotherapy: Penicillins (amoxicillin), rifampicin (TB), metronidazole, fluconazole.
Dental: Dentifrices, mummifying agents, styptics, candidiasis treatment, ANUG treatment.
Systemic: Adrenaline, beta blockers, ACE inhibitors, diuretics, insulin/metformin, corticosteroids.
GIT: Peptic ulcer drugs (PPIs / H2 blockers).

chapters.blurb: Basic concepts, usually as short notes.

subjects.name: Dental Materials
mustRead: Impression Materials: Elastomers (addition silicone) and hydrocolloids (alginate/agar).
Cements: GIC is the most critical.
Gypsum Products: Setting expansion (hygroscopic) and plaster vs stone.
Resins: Acrylic porosity, polymerization stages, composites (hybrid).
Amalgam: High copper amalgam & trituration.
Metallurgy: Casting defects (porosity), soldering/welding, base metal alloys.
Ceramics: Strengthening mechanisms and classification.
Gold: Direct filling gold (mat/foil).
